rule: A search term that spent at least the threshold and never converted is waste: add it as a negative keyword.
formula: conversions = 0 AND cost >= min_cost AND not brand
threshold: $20 (--min-cost), or about the same in the export's currency
data_needed: Search terms report: search term, cost, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: the fixed dollar threshold becomes the spend level at which zero-conversion terms stopped converting later, backtested per vertical on the gold set.
notes: A fixed dollar amount ignores CPA: $20 is about 1x CPA at a $20 CPA but 0.1x at $200. Since 2026-09-29 the dollar threshold only decides what is worth listing; the waste model's 90% bar (stw-waste-model) decides what to add as a negative.

rule: Search terms that match the brand, or a close typo of it, are never waste and never suggested as negatives.
formula: term contains a brand name (3+ letters) OR a word with similarity >= 0.8 to the brand's first word (5+ letters)
threshold: similarity 0.8; first word 5+ letters; names 3+ letters
data_needed: Search terms report + --brand names
notes: On the first real export, brand terms would otherwise have topped the waste list; adding them as negatives hands those searches to competitors.

rule: Waste in Performance Max and other automated campaigns is listed apart from Search: there, negatives only block Search and Shopping ads, and they go in the campaign (up to 10,000) or an account-level list.
formula: campaign type is not Search
threshold: 10,000 negatives per campaign (Google)
data_needed: Search terms report with the Campaign type column
notes: Corrected 2026-09-29 from Google's own pages: the report used to say Performance Max only takes account-level negatives.

rule: A single zero-conversion search term only counts as proven waste once the waste model is 90% sure it converts at less than half the account's rate; below that, judge recurring words, not single terms.
formula: fewest clicks with no conversion at which P(bad) >= 0.9 (see stw-waste-model); past 2,000 clicks the account's terms are called alike
threshold: 90% sure; bad = under half the account rate
data_needed: Search terms report: search term, cost, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: the prior's spread borrowed from similar live accounts, so small accounts get a sensible bar.
notes: Replaced the 1-in-5 bad-luck rule on 2026-09-29 after a backtest on live accounts.

rule: Every zero-conversion waste term gets the chance that it truly converts at less than half the account's rate. Add it as a negative only at 90% or more; below that it may just be unlucky.
formula: P(bad) = regularized incomplete beta I at 0.5 x account rate of (alpha + conversions, beta + clicks - conversions); alpha and beta fit by beta-binomial maximum likelihood on the account's non-brand terms, mean fixed at the account rate
threshold: 90%; prior strength kept between 1 and 10,000
data_needed: Search terms report: clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: shrink the spread toward similar live accounts (a vertical-level prior) and report each rule's backtested result.
notes: Backtested on live accounts, 2025-2026, excluding terms people had already negated: terms at 90%+ later converted at a small fraction of their account's rate, while flags from a fixed dollar threshold converted at close to the normal rate. Thin sample so far: few accounts have terms that reach 90%.

rule: Words and two-word phrases that recur across search terms and never converted are negative keyword candidates, even when each term alone is too small to judge.
formula: n-gram (word of 3+ letters, or two-word phrase, stopwords removed) in >= 3 search terms, total cost >= $5, total conversions = 0; a phrase carrying >= 80% of a word's cost replaces the word
threshold: 3 terms; $5; 0.8; top 10
data_needed: Search terms report: search term, cost, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: a per-vertical list of words that never convert across the gold set, offered as a starter negative list.
notes: Adalysis also flags n-grams with 150+ clicks and no conversions.

rule: A search term that converts, but at more than 3x the account's cost per conversion, is flagged as expensive.
formula: conversions > 0 AND cost >= min_cost AND cost / conversions > 3 x account CPA
threshold: 3x account CPA
data_needed: Search terms report: search term, cost, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: the multiple comes from the spread of converting terms' CPA in the vertical.

rule: A search term with 2 or more conversions at or below the account's cost per conversion that is not a keyword yet should be added as one.
formula: conversions >= 2 AND CPA <= account CPA AND Added/Excluded = None
threshold: 2 conversions
data_needed: Search terms report: search term, cost, clicks, conversions, added/excluded

rule: Compare CPC, CTR, conversion rate and cost per conversion with the industry's published average: a ballpark, never a target.
formula: yours vs average; lower CPC and CPA are better, higher CTR and conversion rate are better
threshold: WordStream / LocaliQ 2026 US search averages, 24 industries
data_needed: Any export with cost, clicks, impressions, conversions
calibration: Paid: replaced by p25 / p50 / p75 from live accounts in the same vertical and currency, only where a cell has enough accounts; otherwise the public average.
notes: Industry cost per lead is used as cost per conversion. US-only, a year averaged, both Google and Microsoft Ads.

rule: A keyword that spent at least the threshold and never converted is listed for review: pause it, lower its bid, or fix its ad and landing page.
formula: conversions = 0 AND cost >= min_cost AND not brand
threshold: $20 (--min-cost), or about the same in the export's currency
data_needed: Keywords report: keyword, match type, cost, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: same calibration as stw-waste, at keyword level.

rule: Brand keywords with zero conversions are never listed for pausing: pausing brand keywords hands those searches to competitors.
formula: brand match (same test as stw-brand-never-waste)
data_needed: Keywords report + --brand names

rule: Show cost, share of cost, conversions and CPA by match type, so budget drifting to broad match is visible.
formula: group by match type: cost, cost / total cost, conversions, cost / conversions
data_needed: Keywords report with match type
calibration: Paid: match-type mix and CPA gap against similar accounts.

rule: Keywords with a Quality Score of 4 or lower usually pay more for the same position; report their cost and share of spend.
formula: quality score <= 4
threshold: Quality Score 4
data_needed: Keywords report with Quality Score
notes: Google calls Quality Score a diagnostic, not a KPI and not an auction input.

rule: A change smaller than 3% is called flat.
formula: |pct_change| < 0.03
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: With fewer than 10 conversions in both periods, CPA movement is noise: do not read it as a trend or act on it.
formula: max(conversions now, conversions before) < 10
threshold: 10 conversions
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Under 50 conversions a period, a conversion move smaller than 10% is one or two events and is called flat.
formula: max(conversions) < 50 AND |conversion change| < 0.10
threshold: 50 conversions; 10%
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: When conversions are zero in either period, the read is a tracking check, not a performance verdict.
formula: conversions now = 0 OR conversions before = 0
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend cut, conversions held within 20% of prior, CPA improved: an efficiency win. Falling conversions here are a good outcome.
formula: spend down AND -0.20 <= conversion change <= 0.03 AND CPA down
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend cut and conversions fell more than 20%, but less than spend, so CPA improved: the cut removed waste first.
formula: spend down AND conversion change < -0.20 AND CPA down
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend, clicks and conversions fell together with CPA within 10%: volume fell because spend fell, not because performance broke.
formula: spend down AND conversions down AND |CPA change| <= 0.10
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend down but conversions fell faster, so CPA rose: the cut removed converting volume, not just waste.
formula: spend down AND conversions down AND CPA up
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend up while conversions fell and CPA rose: more money bought worse traffic, or the funnel broke after the click. The worst pattern.
formula: spend up AND conversions down AND CPA up
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Spend flat, conversions down, CPA up: traffic is similar, so look at the landing page, form, offer or tracking, not targeting.
formula: spend flat AND conversions down AND CPA up
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversions up and CPA down: more output at lower cost.
formula: conversions up AND CPA down
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversions, spend and CPA all up: growth is real but the marginal conversion costs far more than the average.
formula: conversions up AND spend up AND CPA up
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversions up with CPA flat: spend and output grew together at stable efficiency.
formula: conversions up AND CPA flat
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversions flat, CPA up: extra spend or reach returned nothing.
formula: conversions flat AND CPA up
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversions flat, CPA down: efficiency improved without volume changing.
formula: conversions flat AND CPA down
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Impressions up 50% or more while CTR fell to 70% of prior or less: broad matching or audience expansion is buying low-intent reach.
formula: impression change >= 0.50 AND CTR now / CTR before <= 0.70
threshold: +50% reach; CTR at 70% of prior
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Impressions down 30% or more while CTR rose to 130% of prior or more: targeting narrowed and relevance improved.
formula: impression change <= -0.30 AND CTR now / CTR before >= 1.30
threshold: -30% reach; CTR at 130% of prior
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: Conversion rate fell to 70% of prior or less on 200+ clicks: suspect the landing page, offer, tracking or click quality.
formula: CVR now / CVR before <= 0.70 AND clicks now >= 200
threshold: 70% of prior; 200 clicks
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions

rule: When 25% or more of clicks convert, the conversions are engagement actions, not leads or sales: do not read CPA as cost per lead.
formula: conversions / clicks >= 0.25
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions
calibration: Paid: the ceiling comes from the conversion-rate spread of accounts with verified lead or sale tracking in the vertical.

rule: Under 30 conversions a period is too few to judge automated bidding on.
formula: 0 < max(conversions) < 30
threshold: 30 conversions
data_needed: Two-period totals: spend, impressions, clicks, conversions
notes: Google judges Smart Bidding over 30+ days with 30+ conversions (50 for Target ROAS); Target CPA can start with no history.

rule: For seasonal businesses, period over period is the wrong lens: compare with the same period last year before crediting the account.
formula: business model mentions a seasonal word
threshold: seasonal, rafting, ski, charter
data_needed: Business model (meta)

rule: Non-USD accounts are never compared with USD figures.
formula: currency != USD
data_needed: Currency (meta)

rule: A written number counts as traced when it matches a figure from the data at the precision it was written: $1.4k matches 1,361.04, $1,500 does not.
formula: round(fact, precision of the written number) = written number
data_needed: Any audit text + the exports it describes

rule: A number is tied to the nearest metric word within 45 characters; a clause break or a conjunction between them pushes the word further away. A right number on the wrong metric or row is a mismatch.
formula: rank = distance + 25 if a clause break + 10 if and / but / while / versus
threshold: 45 characters
data_needed: Any audit text + the exports it describes

rule: A money figure can only be a cost, a CPC or a CPA, never a count.
formula: money numbers only consider cost, cpc, cpa

rule: A sentence whose direction word contradicts its own numbers is flagged: 'fell from 9% to 14%'.
formula: direction word disagrees with from X to Y

rule: Grade the account on the share of spend that went to search terms costing more than $10 with no conversions in 30 days.
formula: cost of terms with cost > $10 and 0 conversions / total cost
threshold: pass < 5%, warn 5-15%, fail > 15%
data_needed: Search terms report, last 30 days
calibration: Paid: pass and fail bands from the waste-share spread of similar live accounts.
notes: The $10 floor does not scale with CPA or currency.

rule: Compare the CPA of all search terms with the CPA of converting terms only: the ratio shows whether query control is too loose or too tight.
formula: LR = CPA of all search terms / CPA of search terms with 1+ conversion
threshold: 1.0-1.5 too conservative, 1.5-2.0 healthy, 2.0-2.5 too aggressive, > 2.5 mismanaged
data_needed: Search terms report: cost, conversions
calibration: Paid: the healthy band per vertical from live accounts.
notes: By Will Lin and David Rodnitzky (3Q Digital). Optmyzr's skill uses pass 1.5-2.0, warn 2.0-3.0, fail > 3.0 or < 1.5. Computable from the export we already read.

rule: Scan search terms for irrelevant queries routinely; review Quality Score and ad tests weekly, audiences and landing pages monthly.
formula: workflow cadence
threshold: search terms daily; QS and ad tests weekly; audiences and landing pages monthly
data_needed: Change history (date of the last negative added)
notes: A practice, not a formula. Cadence should scale with query volume.

rule: Flag keywords that spent a multiple of target CPA without converting; pause only after checking their search terms, match type, landing page and assisted conversions.
formula: cost >= 2-3 x target CPA AND conversions = 0
threshold: 2-3x target CPA; 4-5x for high-ticket or long sales cycles
data_needed: Keywords report: cost, conversions; target CPA
calibration: Paid: the multiple backtested on live accounts per vertical.
notes: Scales with CPA, unlike our fixed $20. The author says there is no universal testing period.

rule: In low-data accounts, list every keyword with more than 20 clicks and no conversions as a screen, not a pause rule.
formula: clicks > 20 AND conversions = 0
threshold: 20 clicks
data_needed: Keywords report
notes: Optmyzr's default mode estimates clicks per conversion from account history instead, as our stw-clicks-needed does.

rule: Flag keywords whose CPA is far above their ad group's average over 60 days as pause candidates.
formula: keyword CPA / ad group CPA over 60 days
threshold: not published (worked example flagged at +260%)
data_needed: Keywords report (60 days) with ad group
calibration: Paid: the multiple from live accounts.
notes: Opteo publishes only an example, so keep the ratio configurable.

rule: Flag the same keyword text and match type enabled in two or more ad groups when it carries real spend.
formula: same text + match type in >= 2 ad groups AND combined cost > 1% of account cost
threshold: 1% of account spend
data_needed: Keywords report: keyword, match type, ad group, campaign, cost
notes: Do not fix it with Google's auto-applied 'remove redundant keywords'. Runs without the 1% spend condition: a snapshot has no spend.

rule: Measure the share of enabled keywords with no impressions in 30 days, and catch disapproved keywords still enabled.
formula: zero-impression enabled keywords / enabled keywords
threshold: pass < 5% and 0 disapproved; fail > 15% or any disapproved enabled
data_needed: Keywords report (30 days): status, impressions, approval
notes: Optmyzr found no strong link between low-volume keyword counts and performance across 9,000+ accounts. Google auto-pauses keywords with no impressions for 13+ months.

rule: Grade spend-weighted Quality Score and the share of spend on keywords scoring 4 or lower.
formula: sum(QS x cost) / sum(cost); cost on QS <= 4 / total cost
threshold: avg QS pass >= 7, warn 5-6, fail < 5; low-QS spend pass < 10%, warn 10-25%, fail > 25%
data_needed: Keywords report with Quality Score
notes: Extends our live kw-low-quality-score with bands. Ignore QS on low-data and competitor-brand keywords.

rule: Important keywords should hold high exact match impression share; low values point to Quality Score or bids.
formula: exact match impression share
threshold: >= 80% on important keywords; fix QS first when QS < 6
data_needed: Keywords report: search exact match IS, lost IS (rank)
notes: A manual-bidding-era benchmark; low confidence today.

rule: Apply at least one shared negative keyword list across all Search campaigns and keep adding to it.
formula: Search campaigns linked to >= 1 shared negative list
threshold: pass all campaigns; warn < 50%; fail none
data_needed: Shared negative lists and campaign links (API or Editor)
notes: Over-aggressive account-level negatives also cost volume.

rule: A negative keyword must never block an enabled keyword in its own scope.
formula: any negative that matches an enabled keyword in the same ad group, campaign or shared list scope
threshold: any = fail
data_needed: Keywords report + negative keywords export
notes: Negatives do not cover plurals or misspellings automatically, so each variant has to be added. Shared negative lists are not checked yet: the snapshot does not link lists to campaigns.

rule: There is no right number of keywords per ad group: a keyword belongs only if the ad copy describes it.
formula: keyword theme present in the ad group's RSA text
threshold: no maximum
data_needed: Keywords report + Ads report text

rule: Keep brand and non-brand keywords in separate campaigns.
formula: a campaign holds both brand and non-brand keywords (brand test as stw-brand-never-waste)
threshold: any = fail
data_needed: Keywords report: keyword, campaign + --brand
notes: We already have the brand matcher, so this is cheap to add.

rule: Keep Search and Display apart, and flag unexpected setting differences between similar campaigns.
formula: Search campaigns with Display Network on; differing locations, networks, schedules, devices or bid strategies in a campaign group
threshold: any = flag
data_needed: Campaign settings export
notes: The tool has to define a campaign group, for example by naming convention. Live for Search campaigns on the Display Network only.

rule: Campaigns meeting their CPA or ROAS target should not lose much impression share to budget.
formula: Search lost IS (budget) on campaigns at or better than target
threshold: pass < 10%, warn 10-25%, fail > 25%
data_needed: Campaigns report: search lost IS (budget), cost, conversions, value; targets
calibration: Paid: which campaigns count as profitable, from the vertical's CPA spread.

rule: Performance Max needs more monthly conversions than Google's floors before its optimization works well.
formula: conversions per PMax campaign per month
threshold: >= 60 a month
data_needed: Campaigns report (30 days)
notes: Well above Google's 15 to 30 conversion floors.

rule: Change target CPA or ROAS once or twice a month on 30-day data, and never within 14 days of the last change.
formula: days since last target change
threshold: >= 14 days; entities near 140% of target flagged
data_needed: Change history + Campaigns report (30 days)
notes: Smart Bidding needs about 7-14 undisturbed days after a change.

rule: Ad groups should run several active ads so copy can be tested.
formula: ad groups with >= 3 active ads / ad groups
threshold: pass >= 95%, warn 80-95%, fail < 80%
data_needed: Ads report: ad group, status, type
notes: Adalysis finds 5+ ads confuse serving and suggests 2-4 for tests.

rule: Responsive search ads should carry enough headlines and descriptions.
formula: median headlines and descriptions per RSA; share of RSAs under 8 headlines
threshold: pass: median >= 10 headlines and >= 3 descriptions, < 20% under 8; fail: median < 7 or < 3, or >= 50% under 8
data_needed: Ads report or RSA asset export
notes: Adalysis warns 15 headlines and 2 descriptions make 50,000+ combinations, which need a lot of data. The report counts ads under 8 headlines; the median bands are not scored.

rule: Avoid reusing one headline or description across many active ads.
formula: largest share of active ads using one text string
threshold: pass <= 15%, warn 15-40%, fail >= 40%
data_needed: Ads report: text

rule: Judge RSAs on CPA, conversion rate and conversions per impression, not on Ad Strength.
formula: compare CPA and CVR by Ad Strength rating
threshold: Optmyzr study: Average had the best CPA ($12.43), Excellent the worst ($28.68)
data_needed: Ads report: ad strength, impressions, cost, conversions
calibration: Paid: the same comparison on live accounts per vertical.
notes: Study of about 20k accounts.

rule: Avoid fully pinned RSAs; partial pinning did best in Optmyzr's data.
formula: flag RSAs with every position pinned
threshold: study CPA: partial pinning $13.68, full pinning $32.57
data_needed: Ads report or RSA assets: pinned positions

rule: Declare an ad test winner only at enough statistical confidence, more for important keywords.
formula: significance of the difference in the test metric
threshold: >= 90% floor; 95-99% for top keywords and own brand
data_needed: Ads report: impressions, clicks, conversions, value per ad

rule: Do not judge an ad test before each ad has minimum data and at least a week of history.
formula: per ad, for low / mid / high traffic
threshold: impressions 350 / 750 / 1,000; clicks 300 / 500 / 1,000; conversions 7 / 13 / 20; >= 7 days
data_needed: Ads report with date range
notes: Numbers as published (2015); apply the one that matches the test metric (our reading).

rule: Pick the ad test metric by goal: conversions per impression for leads, revenue per impression for sales, CTR only for traffic.
formula: CPI = conversions / impressions = CTR x CVR
data_needed: Ads report
notes: CPI rewards both CTR and conversion rate.

rule: Each active Search campaign should have enough sitelinks, callouts and structured snippets.
formula: count by asset type per campaign
threshold: >= 4 sitelinks, >= 4 callouts, >= 1 structured snippet
data_needed: Assets report: type, level, status
notes: Assets can sit at account, campaign or ad group level.

rule: Top-spend final URLs must resolve and load fast on mobile.
formula: HTTP status and mobile load time per top-spend final URL
threshold: pass < 2.5 s, warn 2.5-4 s, fail > 4 s; any 404 or 5xx fails
data_needed: Ads report final URLs + a crawler
notes: Needs a crawler or PageSpeed call: not in exports, and it breaks the offline promise.

rule: Keep a short list of primary conversion actions that match business goals; micro-conversions go to secondary.
formula: count of primary conversion actions
threshold: pass 1-3; fail > 5 or all set up the same
data_needed: Conversion actions export

rule: Primary conversion actions should share counting, windows and attribution, and call conversions need a minimum call length.
formula: mixed windows or attribution across primary actions; call actions counting any call
threshold: suggested 30 or 60 seconds minimum call
data_needed: Conversion actions export: windows, attribution, call length

rule: Target people in or regularly in your locations, not people merely interested in them.
formula: geo target type per campaign
threshold: pass Presence; fail if most campaigns use Presence or interest
data_needed: Campaign settings: geo target type

rule: Keep device bid adjustments modest and backed by device conversion data.
formula: bid adjustment per device vs device CPA
threshold: pass within +/-20% with data; fail -100% or extremes without data
data_needed: Campaigns report by device + adjustments

rule: Lead-gen campaigns running 24/7 should schedule or adjust hours that convert poorly.
formula: conversion rate by hour vs average
threshold: no published number
data_needed: Campaigns report by hour and day
calibration: Paid: the off-hours cut-off from live lead-gen accounts.
notes: Low confidence: the source gives no threshold.

rule: Keep auto-apply off for keyword-removal recommendations such as removing redundant or non-serving keywords.
formula: auto-apply on for keyword removal; keywords removed by Google in change history
threshold: any = flag
data_needed: Recommendation auto-apply settings (API) + change history
notes: Removed Search keywords hand their queries to PMax. Optmyzr saw an auto-removed brand keyword go from 7 conversions to 0.

rule: Attach audiences to Search campaigns in Observation mode, and keep a fresh Customer Match list.
formula: Search campaigns with audiences; Customer Match list size and age
threshold: fail no audiences; pass >= 1 list with 1,000+ records refreshed within 90 days
data_needed: Audience report + Customer Match lists

rule: Find converting PMax search terms that are not exact keywords in Search, and move them into Search.
formula: PMax search term with conversions AND not an exact-match keyword in any Search campaign
threshold: any = flag
data_needed: PMax search terms report + Keywords report
notes: Experts disagree on how much it matters: Adalysis saw PMax win 61% of overlapping impressions; Optmyzr (503 accounts) found no CVR difference in most overlaps.

rule: PMax picks up queries where Search is ineligible or weaker, so compare their settings and budgets.
formula: budget-limited Search, narrower Search geo or schedule, extra Search exclusions, or a looser PMax target
threshold: any = flag
data_needed: Campaign settings + Campaigns report

rule: Review PMax search terms like Search ones and exclude irrelevant queries on evidence.
formula: qualitative
data_needed: PMax search terms report
notes: Optmyzr (Jun 2025): campaign-level PMax negatives are now allowed, up to 10,000. 58% of advertisers saw flat or better results with no exclusions.

rule: Break PMax cost and conversions out by channel to find channels that spend without return.
formula: cost share and CPA per channel
threshold: no published cut-off
data_needed: PMax channel performance report
calibration: Paid: normal channel mix per vertical from live accounts.

rule: Check how much of total spend sits in PMax.
formula: PMax cost / total cost
threshold: 10-25% went with the best CVR and CPA; > 50% with mixed results
data_needed: Campaigns report: cost by campaign type
notes: A correlation across accounts, not a causal rule.

rule: Each PMax asset group should have an audience signal and search themes, but judge assets on results, not completeness.
formula: asset groups with >= 1 audience signal and search themes
threshold: pass all
data_needed: Asset groups export
notes: Optmyzr found search themes gave mixed results and text-only asset sets often beat full creative sets.

rule: Exclude sites, apps and YouTube placements that build up cost without converting, ideally at account level.
formula: placements with cost and 0 conversions after a monitoring period
threshold: no published number
data_needed: Placement report
calibration: Paid: the monitoring spend per vertical.

rule: Flag product titles that bury key information, products missing identifiers, and disapproved products.
formula: title length; missing GTIN / MPN, brand, price, availability; disapproved
threshold: titles > 40 characters flagged
data_needed: Merchant Center feed + product status

rule: Every product should sit in exactly one active campaign, and Shopping campaigns should have negative keywords.
formula: products in 0 or > 1 active campaigns; Shopping campaigns with 0 negatives; empty product groups
threshold: any = flag
data_needed: Shopping report by item ID + negatives

rule: Keep exact and phrase match as the core and use broad match for discovery: exact leads on efficiency.
formula: CPA and conversion rate by match type
threshold: Optmyzr study: exact most efficient, phrase the workhorse, broad adds volume at higher cost
data_needed: Keywords report with match type
calibration: Paid: match-type CPA gaps on live accounts per vertical.
notes: 30k accounts, May 2026. Our live kw-match-type-mix already prints the numbers this rule needs.

rule: Group keywords into tightly themed ad groups; fold single-keyword ad groups into themed ones so Smart Bidding works on pooled data.
threshold: flag ad groups with exactly 1 keyword; one narrow theme per ad group (qualitative)
data_needed: Keywords report: keyword, ad group, campaign; Campaigns report: bid strategy
notes: No keywords-per-ad-group number given. Counterweight: Google warns reorganizing wipes accumulated history (answer 6372655), so restructure deliberately.

rule: Do not split the same keyword across match types or ad groups; keep a theme's match types in one ad group and simplify to broad match under Smart Bidding.
threshold: count of keyword texts present in more than 1 match type or ad group = 0 (Smart Bidding campaigns)
data_needed: Keywords report: keyword text, match type, ad group, bid strategy
notes: Google says there is no extra benefit to multiple match types with Smart Bidding; cites 62% of Smart Bidding advertisers using broad as primary (Google data 2023). Google's incentive: broader reach.

rule: Remove device-based campaign segmentation (segment by business objective instead) and clean up duplicate and non-serving keywords.
threshold: 0 device-split campaign clones; 0 duplicate keywords; non-serving keywords (0 impressions or Low search volume) removed; lookback window is ours
data_needed: Campaigns report: device targeting/bid adjustments; Keywords report: status, impressions
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Smart Bidding already accounts for device. Live for non-serving keywords; duplicates run under kw-duplicates.

rule: Broad match keywords should only run in campaigns that use Smart Bidding.
threshold: if enabled broad keywords > 0 then bid strategy in {Target CPA, Target ROAS, Maximize conversions, Maximize conversion value}
data_needed: Keywords report: match type; Campaigns report: bid strategy type
notes: Google calls this critical. Broader match types already capture narrower types' queries.

rule: Negative keywords do not match close variants, so add synonyms and singular/plural forms explicitly.
threshold: each key negative theme also covers plural/singular and synonym forms (qualitative)
data_needed: Negative keywords: ad group, campaign, shared lists, account-level
notes: Words after the 16th word of a long query are not checked against negatives. Google also warns too many negatives can shrink reach.

rule: Keep one global account-level negative list for terms irrelevant to the whole business; it applies to Search and Shopping inventory incl. Performance Max.
threshold: account-level negatives present; count <= 1,000
data_needed: Account settings: account-level negative keywords (API: customer_negative_criterion)
notes: Covers Search, PMax, App, Shopping, Smart, Local search/shopping inventory. Separate cap of 1,000 excluded content keywords for YouTube/Display. 'Single global list' advice is on answer 2453972.

rule: Stay within negative keyword capacity and consolidate before hitting caps.
threshold: shared lists <= 20 per account; <= 5,000 keywords per list; <= 10,000 negatives per campaign; Display/Video: max 1,000 negatives applied
data_needed: Shared library: negative keyword lists; campaign negatives
notes: Same page: max 3 enabled RSAs per ad group; 100 PMax campaigns per account.

rule: Review the search terms report; add irrelevant terms as negatives and use it to refine keywords and match types.
threshold: irrelevant terms with spend not excluded (tool proxy, ours: cost > 0, conversions = 0, no matching negative)
data_needed: Search terms report: term, match type, cost, conversions, added/excluded
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Low-volume terms are hidden for privacy, so the report undercounts. Google gives no review cadence.

rule: Each RSA needs at least 3 headlines and 2 descriptions and can hold 15 headlines and 4 descriptions; fill toward the maximum.
threshold: headlines >= 3 (target 15); descriptions >= 2 (target 4); headline <= 30 chars, description <= 90, path <= 15
data_needed: Ads report: RSA headlines and descriptions per ad
notes: Ad Strength page (9921843) says to provide as many as you can. Up to 3 headlines show at once.

rule: Run at least 2 RSAs rated Good or Excellent in every ad group.
threshold: 2 <= enabled RSAs per ad group <= 3 (hard cap 3); Ad Strength in {Good, Excellent}
data_needed: Ads report: ad type, status, Ad Strength (API: ad_group_ad.ad_strength)
notes: Google averages: +6.6% conversions going 1 to 2 RSAs, +3.7% going 2 to 3, +15% going Poor to Excellent (answer 12158267 says 12%). Google: Ad Strength is a feedback tool, not used for Ad Rank, Quality Score or auctions. Ad Strength is shown, not judged.

rule: Pin headlines or descriptions only when necessary; if you must pin, pin several unique assets to the same position.
threshold: flag positions with exactly 1 pinned asset; minimize share of pinned assets
data_needed: Ads report: asset pinned field (API: ad_text_asset.pinned_field)
notes: Pinning cuts the combinations the system can test.

rule: Provide enough sitelinks: at least 6 with descriptions for high-volume campaigns and ad groups, at least 4 at account level.
threshold: sitelinks eligible per high-volume campaign/ad group >= 6; account-level >= 4; >= 2 needed to show; link text <= 25 chars
data_needed: Assets report: sitelinks by level, with descriptions
notes: Desktop shows up to 6, mobile up to 8. For Good+ Ad Strength Google also asks for 4+ image assets and business name plus logo (answer 9921843). The 6-for-busy-campaigns part is stated in the report, not checked.

rule: Add structured snippets with enough values per header and more than one header set.
threshold: values per header >= 3 (required), aim >= 4; header sets > 1
data_needed: Assets report: structured snippets header and values

rule: Use Quality Score (1-10) and its three components as a diagnostic to locate weak ads and landing pages, not as a KPI to optimize or average.
threshold: flag spend-weighted keywords where expected CTR, ad relevance or landing page experience = Below average; never score accounts on average QS
data_needed: Keywords report: Quality Score and 3 components (API: ad_group_criterion.quality_info)
notes: Not an auction input. Compared with other advertisers on the exact same searches over the last 90 days; shows a dash when data is thin.

rule: Use Search lost IS (budget) to spot budget caps and Search lost IS (rank) to spot Ad Rank losses.
threshold: lost IS (budget) > 0 while on CPA/ROAS target = budget opportunity; limited by budget and missing target = raise budget or use Maximize conversions; trigger level (e.g., > 10%) is ours
data_needed: Campaigns report: Search IS, Search lost IS (budget), Search lost IS (rank)
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Lost IS (budget) is campaign-level only. Budget-limited guidance is from answer 10276704. Google says small IS fluctuations need no action (answer 2497703).

rule: Daily spend can reach 2x the average daily budget; monthly charges are capped at 30.4x the daily budget.
threshold: day cost <= 2 x daily budget; month cost <= 30.4 x daily budget
data_needed: Campaigns report by day: cost, budget
notes: Explains overspend days. Maximize strategies sharing a budget with other strategies show 'Misconfigured' status (answer 6263057).

rule: Judge Smart Bidding only over windows with enough conversions, such as a month or longer.
threshold: window >= 30 days AND conversions >= 30 (>= 50 for Target ROAS); below this report 'insufficient data'
data_needed: Campaigns report by date: conversions, value, cost, bid strategy
notes: Target CPA page (6268632): tCPA can start with no history; evaluate last 30 days with >= 30 conversions; recommended tCPA = 30-day average CPA.

rule: Target ROAS needs minimum recent conversion volume, which differs by campaign type.
threshold: Search/Shopping >= 15 conv in 30 days; Display >= 15 valued conv in 30 days; Demand Gen >= 50 in 35 days with >= 10 in last 7 (or 100 across DG); App >= 10/day
data_needed: Campaigns report: conversions and conversion value, last 7/30/35 days
notes: Eligibility floor, not a performance floor; evaluation guidance asks for 50 conversions (7065882).

rule: After a new strategy or a change to settings, targets or campaign composition, allow the learning period before judging results.
threshold: no verdict until >= 1-2 conversion cycles and >= 7-14 days after the change (formula combines two pages)
data_needed: Change history; bid strategy status (Learning); Days to conversion
notes: The 7-14 day figure is on 'About conversion measurement' (answer 1722022). Learning continues after the status clears.

rule: Change Target CPA or ROAS gradually: about 20% at a time and a week between changes.
threshold: |target change| <= 20% per step; >= 7 days between steps unless > 100 conversions/day
data_needed: Change history: bid strategy target edits with dates; conversions per day
notes: Other types: Search, avoid multiple target changes within one conversion cycle (10433846); Demand Gen/YouTube 5-10%/week, max 15%; Shopping/PMax promos 30% steps with 1-2 cycles between (15624876).

rule: Since 17 Aug 2026, budget-limited tCPA/tROAS campaigns that beat their target are steered toward the target, so loose targets now cost efficiency.
threshold: flag target-based campaigns whose last-30-day CPA is well below target CPA (or ROAS well above target); gap cut-off (e.g., 20%) is ours
data_needed: Campaigns report: target CPA/ROAS vs actual CPA/ROAS, budget status
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Changed 2026. Covers Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, Display, Hotel, Travel; not App, Video reach/views. Google's Bid Target Adjustment Tool helps re-set targets.

rule: Use seasonality adjustments only for short events with a major expected conversion-rate change.
threshold: duration ideally 1-7 days; flag > 14 days
data_needed: Bid strategy advanced controls (API: bidding_seasonality_adjustment)
notes: Smart Bidding already handles normal seasonality.

rule: Apply data exclusions quickly when conversion tracking breaks; do not use them for old or long-running issues.
threshold: exclusion applied within ~7 days of outage; not for issues older than 14 days (Search/Display) or 60 days (Shopping)
data_needed: Data exclusions (API: bidding_data_exclusion); daily conversions series
notes: Backfill only 5+ days after an exclusion (answer 10370710).

rule: Enhanced CPC stopped working for Search and Display campaigns in the week of 31 Mar 2025; unmigrated campaigns now run on Manual CPC.
threshold: 0 campaigns on ECPC; Manual CPC campaigns with conversion tracking flagged for review (review flag is ours)
data_needed: Campaigns report: bid strategy type
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Changed 2025; applies to Display too. Google suggests Max conversions/tCPA or Max conv. value/tROAS.

rule: Campaigns on Manual CPC or Maximize clicks bid for clicks, not conversions: move them to Maximize conversions or Target CPA once conversion tracking works.
formula: bid strategy is Manual CPC, Maximize clicks or Enhanced CPC
data_needed: Campaign bid strategies (snapshot or Editor export)
notes: Google's Enhanced CPC page points to these strategies; flagging click bidding is our call.

rule: Fill every asset group with all asset types at recommended counts and aim for Good or Excellent Ad Strength.
threshold: headlines >= 11 (max 15, one <= 15 chars); long headlines >= 2; descriptions >= 4; images >= 4 at 1.91:1, >= 4 at 1:1, >= 2 at 4:5; square logo >= 1; video >= 1; wait 2-3 weeks before replacing low performers
data_needed: Asset group assets report: counts by field type and ratio; asset group Ad Strength
notes: Pages disagree: optimization tips page (11385582) asks for 15 headlines, 5 descriptions, 7 images, 1 video.

rule: Upload your own videos in horizontal, square and vertical; otherwise Google auto-generates videos.
threshold: advertiser video >= 1 per orientation (16:9, 1:1, 9:16); 3 per orientation recommended; 10-60 seconds each
data_needed: Asset group assets: video assets with orientation and source
notes: Specs page (17091269): videos 10 seconds or more, up to 15.

rule: Run new Performance Max campaigns long enough before judging, and let them settle after significant changes.
threshold: campaign age >= 6 weeks before verdict; 1-2 weeks (or 1 conversion cycle) after significant changes; avoid frequent budget, bid strategy or status edits
data_needed: Campaign start date; change history
notes: Same 6-week rule on answer 15624876. Google's incentive: longer runs mean more spend.

rule: Add unique, non-redundant search themes per asset group.
threshold: search themes per asset group <= 50; no near-synonyms (e.g., car vs automobile)
data_needed: Asset group signals: search themes
notes: Same priority as phrase/broad keywords; negatives and exclusions still apply.

rule: An exact-match Search keyword identical to the query beats Performance Max; identical phrase/broad keywords and search themes compete at equal priority.
threshold: for must-own queries (e.g., brand), an identical exact-match keyword exists in a Search campaign
data_needed: Keywords report (exact match); PMax search terms insights
notes: Shopping ad formats can still show alongside the exact-match ad.

rule: Use brand lists as brand exclusions to keep Performance Max off your own brand (when brand runs in Search) or unwanted brands.
threshold: if a brand Search campaign exists, PMax has a brand exclusion list with the own brand (operationalization ours)
data_needed: Campaign settings: brand exclusions (not in standard exports)
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Covers misspellings and subsidiaries better than negatives. In PMax applies to Search and Shopping ads; Shopping can be re-allowed. Adalysis: PMax can still serve brand misspellings, so add them as exact keywords in brand Search.

rule: Performance Max campaign and account-level negatives only block Search and Shopping inventory, not other PMax channels.
threshold: qualitative: do not rely on negatives for YouTube/Display/Gmail safety; use content exclusions
data_needed: PMax campaign negatives; account-level negatives; content exclusions
notes: Negative keyword lists can be attached to PMax.

rule: Final URL expansion is on by default; turn it off when one page is the only conversion path, otherwise exclude non-commercial URLs.
threshold: single-page funnel: FUE off (keep text customization on); FUE on: URL exclusions or rules present (e.g., /blog)
data_needed: Campaign settings: Final URL expansion, URL exclusions; landing pages report
notes: FUE is not supported for store-goal-only campaigns.

rule: Add audience signals (your data, Customer Match, custom segments) to guide learning; they are hints, not targeting limits.
threshold: audience signals per asset group >= 1, ideally first-party (count is ours)
data_needed: Asset group signals: audiences
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: PMax may serve outside the signals if conversion odds are high.

rule: Give PMax enough budget: not below Google's 'Low' suggestion, and extra headroom on key promotion days.
threshold: daily budget >= budget panel 'Low' level; promo days about 3x expected spend (2x target spend with no history)
data_needed: Campaign budget; budget recommendations
notes: 'Low' = minimum recommended is on answer 10724817. Holiday context. Google's incentive: more spend.

rule: Set Demand Gen daily budget to at least 10x target CPA and watch utilization.
threshold: daily budget >= 10 x target CPA; spend <= ~80% of daily budget while on target (higher = budget-constrained)
data_needed: Campaigns report: budget, cost per day, target CPA
notes: Same 10x on 'About Demand Gen campaigns' (13695777). Google calls low budget the top reason new campaigns underperform.

rule: Let Demand Gen campaigns reach 50 conversions before big changes; then change bids slowly and re-evaluate after enough conversions.
threshold: conversions >= 50 before edits or verdicts; bid change 5-10% per week, max +/-15%; wait 30-50 conversions after a change; no conversion goal change on live campaigns
data_needed: Change history; conversions since launch or change
notes: Creative edits trigger policy review (about 24-48 hours).

rule: Start on Maximize conversions and move to tCPA/tROAS after 50 conversions; start tROAS about 20% below recent ROAS.
threshold: conversions >= 50 before switching to tCPA/tROAS; first tROAS ~ 0.8 x last-30-day ROAS
data_needed: Campaigns report: bid strategy, conversions, ROAS (30 days)
notes: tROAS eligibility: 50 conv in 35 days incl. 10 in last 7 (6268637).

rule: For YouTube conversion campaigns: fund enough budget, wait for 50 conversions, merge sparse ad groups, change slowly, and supply all three video orientations.
threshold: target strategies: daily budget >= 10 x tCPA; Maximize: >= $100/day; no verdict before 50 conv; merge ad groups < 30 conv in 30 days; changes 5-10%/week (<= 15%); >= 1 vertical, 1 square, 1 horizontal video
data_needed: Campaigns/ad groups report: budget, conversions (30d), bid strategy; video assets by orientation; change history
notes: $100 floor is stated without currency adjustment. Google claims 40%+ more conversions using 3 of 4 practices (its own data and incentive).

rule: Fill responsive display ad slots and add images in all recommended ratios plus video to improve Ad Strength.
threshold: headlines 5 of 5 (30 chars); long headline 1 (90); descriptions 5 of 5 (90); images >= 1 at 1.91:1 and >= 1 at 1:1 (up to 15, 9:16 optional); logo; video present
data_needed: Ads report: RDA asset counts by type and ratio
notes: Google gives maxima, not a recommended count; 'fill all slots' is our reading of the best practices guide (9823397).

rule: Keep product titles within 150 characters with key details first, and use images of at least 500x500 px without promo overlays or placeholders.
threshold: title length <= 150; image >= 500 x 500 px (enforced from 31 Jan 2027); no promotional text or placeholder images
data_needed: Merchant Center feed: title, image_link, image dimensions
notes: Merchant Center Help. Front-loading and no-overlay guidance is on answer 7380908. New image minimum enforced 2027.

rule: Submit valid GTINs wherever they exist, detailed product categories, unique IDs and titles, and current price and availability.
threshold: GTIN present for every product that has one; google_product_category >= 2-3 levels deep; unique id and title per product
data_needed: Merchant Center feed: gtin, brand, google_product_category, product_type, price, availability
notes: Merchant Center Help. Google cites +20% clicks on average after adding correct GTINs.

rule: Only conversion actions that should drive bidding belong in primary; keep observation-only actions secondary.
threshold: primary actions = business outcomes; micro-actions (page views, clicks) secondary
data_needed: Conversion actions export: primary/secondary, category, goal (API: conversion_action.primary_for_goal)
notes: Primary feeds the Conversions column and bidding; All conversions includes both. Tool cannot know intent, so flag obvious micro-actions.

rule: Count every conversion for sales and one conversion per click for leads.
threshold: category purchase/sale: counting = Every; category lead/sign-up: counting = One
data_needed: Conversion actions export: counting type, category
notes: Google frames each as 'a good choice', not a hard rule.

rule: Use a click-through conversion window long enough to capture the sales cycle.
threshold: click-through window >= 7 days (default 30; range 1-90 by source); view-through default 1 day
data_needed: Conversion actions export: click-through and view-through windows

rule: Use data-driven attribution, the default for most actions; it is most accurate with enough volume.
threshold: attribution model = data-driven; high confidence when >= 200 conversions and >= 2,000 ad interactions in 30 days
data_needed: Conversion actions export: attribution model; Campaigns report: interactions, conversions (30d)
notes: Runs with less data, but with lower precision.

rule: Recent CPA looks inflated and ROAS deflated because late conversions are credited back to the click date.
threshold: exclude the last N days from trend verdicts; N from the account's Days to conversion lag (formula ours)
data_needed: Days to conversion segment; conversion lag report
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Google gives no fixed N.

rule: Turn on enhanced conversions (hashed first-party data) to improve measurement accuracy and bidding.
threshold: enhanced conversions active on primary web and lead actions
data_needed: Conversion settings and Diagnostics: enhanced conversions status
notes: Data is normalized and SHA-256 hashed. Page gives no uplift number.

rule: Send consent signals for EEA traffic via consent mode; conversion modeling needs enough ad clicks.
threshold: EEA traffic: consent mode with ad_user_data and ad_personalization; modeling needs >= 700 ad clicks over 7 days per country and domain grouping
data_needed: Tag diagnostics (consent status); Geo report: clicks by country
notes: Parameters from answer 13695607. Impact reporting needs >= 7 full days (10000067).

rule: Optimization score is Google's 0-100% estimate of how well the account is set up to perform; Google says to apply or dismiss recommendations based on your own goals.
threshold: do not use the score as a success metric (ours); judge each recommendation against account goals
data_needed: Recommendations list; customer.optimization_score (API)
calibration: Paid: the cut-off marked ours comes from live accounts.
notes: Score shifts with ecosystem trends; dismissing recommendations also moves it (9061547); not used by Quality Score. Google's incentive: Partners must keep manager accounts >= 70% (9702452).

rule: Review auto-applied recommendations regularly; auto-apply can change ads, bidding, keywords, targeting and measurement.
threshold: list enabled auto-apply types; review Recommendations History and Change history each cycle
data_needed: Auto-apply settings (UI only); Change history (API: change_event)
notes: Auto-apply never raises budgets, so budget recommendations still need manual review.

rule: Google's default and recommended location option is Presence or interest: people in, regularly in, or interested in your locations.
threshold: geo target type = Presence or interest
data_needed: Campaign settings: geo target type
notes: Google cites about 5% more conversions in some verticals. From the expert research pass, not re-read.

rule: Compare CPC, CTR, conversion rate and CPA with p25 / p50 / p75 of live accounts in the same vertical, currency and campaign type.
formula: account metric vs percentiles of similar accounts
threshold: only cells with enough accounts; otherwise the public average
data_needed: Any export + vertical
notes: Replaces benchmark-industry wherever a cell has enough accounts.

rule: Set the zero-conversion threshold from what happened next on live accounts, not from one number for everyone.
formula: spend multiple of CPA after which zero-conversion terms stopped converting later
threshold: backtested per vertical
data_needed: Search terms report
notes: Replaces the fixed thresholds in stw-waste and kw-zero-conv-vs-target-cpa. First backtest done 2026-09-29 (private); next: a vertical-level prior for small accounts.

rule: Start every account in a vertical with the words that never converted across live accounts in it.
formula: n-gram themes pooled across the vertical, zero conversions everywhere
threshold: min accounts per vertical
data_needed: Search terms report + vertical

rule: Label each rule with what happened when people followed it: CPA and conversions over the next 30 and 60 days.
formula: outcome after the change vs untouched lookalikes
threshold: tested on N accounts
data_needed: Change history + before / after exports
